terms.latin: haec fābula significat (+ acc. and inf.)
terms.gloss: this story means (that …): the moral of the story is …
terms.grammar: fābula (or fābella) as subject of significat, indicat, or admonet; the lesson follows as accusative and infinitive, or a bare infinitive
evidence: Phaedr. 2.8.27–28: haec significat fābula dominum vidēre plūrimum in rēbus suīs
Phaedr. 3.17.13: nihil agere quod nōn prōsit fābella admonet
terms.comment: Latin says what the story teaches rather than naming its moral: Phaedrus opens or closes his fables with haec fābula significat, fābella indicat, fābella admonet. We have found no classical noun for the moral of a fable, so the verb stands as the answer. “What’s the moral?” is Quid haec fābula significat?.

phrases.english: What’s the moral of the story?

phrases.latin: haec significat fābula dominum vidēre plūrimum in rēbus suīs
phrases.english: the moral of this fable is that the master sees most in his own affairs

phrases.latin: nihil agere quod nōn prōsit fābella admonet
phrases.english: the moral of the little fable: do nothing that does no good
